Rashi on Shabbat 97a:10:1.hebrew: או דילמא למעלה מי' פליגי - ומשום הכי פליגי ופטרי רבנן, דאין כאן אויר רה"ר, וזורק ממושיט לא ילפינן, ורבי עקיבא יליף. וסיפא רבנן קאמרי לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:10:1.english: Or perhaps they are disagreeing [regarding] above ten [handbreadths] - And for this reason they disagree and the Rabbis exempt [him], since there is no airspace of a public domain here, and we do not derive throwing from passing, whereas Rabbi Akiva derives [it]. And the Rabbis state the latter clause [of the Mishnah].

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:11:1.hebrew: ועובר גרסינן, מרה"י לרה"י ועובר ברשות הרבים עצמה - ולא גרסינן ברישא הזורק:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:11:1.english: We read [the text as] "and it passes": "from a private domain to a private domain, and it passes through the public domain itself" - and we do not read "one who throws" at the beginning.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:12:1.hebrew: והא אמר ר' אלעזר - בהמצניע, ויליף ממשא בני קהת דארון:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:12:1.english: And didn't Rabbi Elazar say - In [the chapter] Hamatzni'a, and he derives [it] from the burden of the sons of Kehat, of the Ark.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:12:2.hebrew: אלא לאו בזורק - מיירי מתניתא כי מתניתין, וקתני בברייתא עצמה. ובהא הוא דמחייב ר' עקיבא, משום דנקלטה באוירו של רה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:12:2.english: Rather, isn’t [it] with throwing - The baraita is speaking like our Mishnah, and it teaches [this] in the baraita itself. And it is in this [case] that Rabbi Akiva holds [him] liable, because it is contained in the airspace of the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:12:3.english: Above ten [handbreadths] - For he derives throwing from handing over.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:14:1.hebrew: ופליגא דרב חלקיה - הא דר' אלעזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:14:1.english: And [it] disagrees with Rav Ḥilkiya - This [statement] of Rabbi Elazar.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:14:2.hebrew: תוך שלשה דברי הכל חייב - ואע"ג דלא נח, מודו דכמונח דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:14:2.english: Within three [handbreadths], everyone agrees [one is] liable - Even though it did not come to rest, they agree that it is considered as having come to rest.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:14:3.english: Exempt - For we do not derive throwing from handing over.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:14:4.english: We have come to the dispute - And [this refers to the dispute] regarding [the principle that] an object caught [in the airspace] is as though it were placed [on the ground].

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:15:1.hebrew: משום שבות - שזרק מרשותו לרשות חבירו, ולאו משום הפסק רה"ר, דהוא הדין נמי אם היתה אצלו, עד שיערבו:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:15:1.english: Due to rabbinic decree - [This refers to a case] where he threw from his [private] domain to his fellow's [private] domain, and not because of the interposition of the public domain, for the same law applies even if it were next to him, until they make an eruv.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:15:2.hebrew: ואם היו - שתיהן הרשויות שלו, מותר לכתחילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:15:2.english: And if [they] were - both domains [were] his, it is permitted from the outset.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:16:1.hebrew: אסור לזרוק מזה לזה - ואפילו הן שלו, דאי משלו לשל חבירו לא הוה שרי שמואל:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:16:1.english: It is prohibited to throw from this [one] to that [one] - And even [when] they are his [own], for if [it were] from his [domain] to his fellow's [domain], Shmuel would not have permitted [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:16:3.hebrew: דמדלי חד ומתתי חד - דמתוך כך צריך לאמן ידו מגבוה לנמוך או מנמוך לגבוה, טריד בה ודילמא לא זריק על הגג, ונופל לרה"ר ואתי לאתויי. ולהכי נקט ואתי לאתויי, דאילו משום נפילת רה"ר ליכא חיוב חטאת, דמתעסק הוא אצל הוצאה, דלא נתכוון לזרוק לרה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:16:3.english: Where one is elevated and one is low - For because of this, he must aim his hand from high to low or from low to high; [thus] he is preoccupied with it, and perhaps he will not throw [it] onto the roof, and it will fall into the public domain and he will come to bring it [in]. And this is why [the Gemara] stated "and he will come to bring it": for regarding [its] falling into the public domain [itself], there is no liability for a sin offering, since he is acting without intent with respect to carrying out, as he did not intend to throw [it] into the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:17:1.hebrew: כלבוד דמי - דרשות שאינו גבוה ג', בטל אצל רה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:17:1.english: Is considered lavud - For a domain that is not three [handbreadths] high is nullified with respect to the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:17:2.english: He said to him - It is [a matter of] logical reasoning.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:17:3.hebrew: לפי שאי אפשר - להחליק רה"ר מגבשושית, כאילו נלקטו במלקט ורהיטני — פלי"ינה (מקצועה) בלע"ז, והן בשני גווני כלים של עץ וברזל חד נעוץ בתוכו, ובהן משוה פני רוחב הקרש ומחליקה. הלכך, גבשושיות נמי רה"ר:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:17:3.english: Because it is impossible - to smooth the public domain of mounds, as though they were cleared with a malket and rahitani — plaine (a plane) in Old French, and they are two kinds of wooden tools with a sharp iron [blade] inserted inside it, and with them one evens the surface of the width of the board and smooths it. Therefore, mounds are also [considered part of] the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:18:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - אי מסברא, אפילו ג' נמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:18:1.english: He said to him - If [it is] based on reasoning, even three [handbreadths] as well.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:18:2.hebrew: המשלשל - מתחיל לארוג דופני הסוכה בערב כלפי מעלה, ומשלשל ובא כלפי מטה:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:18:2.english: One who lowers - [He] begins to weave the walls of the sukkah with the weft toward the top, and continues lowering [them] toward the bottom.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:18:4.hebrew: אם גבוהות מן הארץ ג' טפחים פסולה, הא פחות מג' כשרה - דאמרינן לבוד, כמי שנכפף עליהן ונשלמו עד למטה; הכא לאו טעמא דתילקט הוא. נראה לי דהכי גרסינן: מאי איכא למימר:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:18:4.english: If they are three handbreadths high from the ground, [it is] invalid; thus, [if] less than three, [it is] valid - For we say [it is] lavud, as though [the wall] were bent over them and [the walls] were completed down to the bottom; here it is not the reason of "it will be leveled." It appears to me that this is how we read [the text]: "What is there to say?"

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:19:1.english: There, [it is] because it is a partition that goats pass through - And in less than three [handbreadths], there is no passing through of goats.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:19:2.hebrew: תינח למטה, למעלה מאי איכא למימר - למעלה, היכא דאמרינן לבוד למעלה בכמה דוכתין, כגון מקיפין ג' חבלים דעירובין (דף טז:), וכגון שהרחיק את הסיכוך מן הדפנות ג' טפחים, פסולה (סוכה דף יז.):
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:19:2.english: It works out well below; above, what is there to say - Above, where we say [the principle of] lavud [applies] above in several places — such as [in the case of] surrounding [an area with] three ropes in Eruvin (16b), and such as [the case where] one distanced the sekhakh from the walls [by] three handbreadths, [in which case] it is invalid (Sukkah 17a).

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:1:1.hebrew: ואלא הא גמיר גזירה שוה - וא"כ לא כסתו התורה, דהוה ליה כמפורש. ומשני: רבי יהודה בן בתירא לא גמרה, ואין אדם דן ג"ש מעצמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:1:1.english: However, didn't he learn a verbal analogy? - And if so, the Torah did not conceal him, for it is as though [it were] explicit. And [the Gemara] answers: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira did not learn it, and a person cannot expound a verbal analogy on his own.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:1:3.hebrew: מהיכן הוה - באיזו חטא מת? דכתיב "כי בחטאו מת":
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:1:3.english: From where was [it] - Through which sin did he die? For it is written, "for he died in his own sin."

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:1:4.hebrew: מויעפילו - ויעפילו לעלות וגו', שלא הרשיע כ"כ כחילול שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:1:4.english: From “And they presumed” - “And they presumed to ascend, etc.” [Numbers 14:44], for he did not act so wickedly as [to commit] desecration of the Sabbath.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:20:1.english: As though [it is] full - Because it is dark and full of vapor.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:20:2.english: However, [if] it is not covered - Such as a courtyard.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:21:1.english: And it was difficult for him - Regarding that which his teacher taught him.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:3:1.english: That he turned from his leprosy - He had already been healed.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:6:1.english: And behold, his hand was leprous - That is, [he was] smitten in his body.

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:6:2.hebrew: ויוציאה והנה ידו - אחר היציאה מצורעת כשלג, ובמדה טובה כתיב "מחיקו והנה שבה":
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:6:2.english: And he took it out and behold, his hand - [It was only] after taking [it] out [that it was] leprous like snow, whereas regarding the attribute of beneficence it is written, "from his bosom and behold, it had returned."

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:7:1.hebrew: נס בתוך נס - לאחר שחזר ונעשה מטה, בלען, ולא כשהוא תנין, דלא כתיב ״ויבלע תנין אהרן״:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:7:1.english: A miracle within a miracle - After it turned back and became a staff, it swallowed them, and not while it was a serpent, for it is not written, "and Aaron's serpent swallowed."

Rashi on Shabbat 97a:9:1.hebrew: ולא ילפינן זורק ממושיט - שהיה בעבודת הלוים למעלה מעשרה, מרשות היחיד לרשות היחיד ורשות הרבים באמצע. וסיפא דקתני הזורק פטור והמושיט חייב, דברי הכל היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 97a:9:1.english: And we do not derive throwing from passing - which was in the service of the Levites above ten [handbreadths], from a private domain to a private domain with a public domain in the middle. And the latter clause [of the Mishnah], which teaches: "One who throws is exempt, and one who passes is liable," is [the opinion of] everyone.

Tosafot on Shabbat 97a:1:1.hebrew: גזירה שוה לא גמיר - ואם תאמר: וליגמר מר' עקיבא, שהוא קבלה מרבו? ואור"ת: שהיה להם בקבלה מנין ג"ש שבכל התורה, וזו היתה יתירה על החשבון; לפיכך לא קיבלה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 97a:1:1.english: "He did not learn a verbal analogy" - And if you ask: let him learn [it] from Rabbi Akiva, who received it from his teacher? And Rabbeinu Tam says that they had by tradition the number of verbal analogies in the entire Torah, and this one was in excess of the count; therefore he did not accept it.
